title: Different When It's Silent
description: New Tricky, three decades into a catalogue still defined by smoke, hush, and bruised trip, hop. He has rarely sounded comfortable on a record, and there is no reason to expect he starts now.

title: Different When It's Silent
description: New Tricky, almost three decades on from Maxinquaye and still circling the same smoke, blackened trip, hop he made his own. Sparse metadata at this stage, but the register is rarely a mystery with him.

title: Hymnal (Resung)
label: 7K - a division of K7 Music GmbH
description: Lyra Pramuk returns to her vocal, as, instrument terrain for 7K!, revisiting the Hymnal material in reworked form. Her processed choral layering remains the whole palette, no percussion, no scaffolding, just voice as architecture.

title: Thirst (2026 Remaster)
label: Clock DVA under exclusive license to Mute Artists Ltd.
description: Mute picks up the 1981 Clock DVA record for a 2026 remaster, cleaning up the Sheffield outfit's paranoid post, punk jazz before it curdled into the colder electronics they're better remembered for. For anyone who files Cabaret Voltaire and 23 Skidoo next to each other.

title: Without References / Cindy Van Acker (Ricardo Villalobos Variations)
label: Latency
description: Villalobos turns up on Latency alongside Tokyo percussion unit goat, the kind of pairing the label has been quietly engineering for a while. Expect his variations to stretch the source material well past its original shape.

title: If This Is It
description: DJ Seinfeld returns to the long, form, the format that has always suited his lovelorn house better than the single. Expect the same diary, entry sentimentality he has built a decade on, pitched somewhere near Ross From Friends if you need an aisle.

title: Somewhere Good
label: World of Echo
description: The Bristol trio return to World of Echo, where their particular dialect of hushed song, form, jazz drift and tape, room electronics has always sat comfortably. Stays close to the spoken, aside intimacy that made the earlier EPs travel.

title: Inferno
label: Warp Records
description: The Sandison brothers back on Warp, still trading in the same weather, damaged tape hiss and decaying pastoral synthwork that has defined them since Music Has the Right. Nothing announces itself; everything settles.

title: Inferno (Continuous Mix)
description: A continuous, mix single from the Sandison brothers, who have spent three decades refining the same hazy, half, corroded approach to melodic electronics. Long, form rather than track, by, track, which is the format their work has always rewarded.

title: Paradessence
label: RVNG Intl.
description: The Portland duo return to RVNG with another set of synthetic ambient assembled from MIDI, era textures and translation errors. Same patient, slightly uncanny register their listeners have come to expect from the label.

title: Opponent Stims
description: Clark in album mode again, which over the past two decades has meant restless, percussive electronics that rarely sit in one mood for long. Sparse details so far, but his Warp, era register is the safe assumption.

title: Pace pe pământ
description: New Moin, the Raime offshoot that has spent the last few years dragging post, hardcore guitar shapes into AD 93's grey, toned orbit. Expect the same uneasy interplay of live drums, scraped six, strings and half, buried voices.

title: Mind Abandon
label: Planet Mu
description: Ital Tek back on Planet Mu, still working the seam between cinematic bass weight and frayed, half, dissolved electronics he has been carving out since Bodied. Filed close to the label's Kuedo corner.

title: Music for Existing
description: Martyn returns to long, form, which usually means his particular read on broken techno, dub, and the slower edges of UK bass gets room to stretch. Label details are still thin, but his back catalogue is the reference point.

title: Now You Exist
description: Axel Willner returns under the Field name, the project long synonymous with looping micro, house stretched into something close to ambient. No label confirmed yet, but the sonic register is well established by now.

title: Loud Bloom
label: Rabid Records under exclusive license to dh2
description: One half of The Knife returning with a full, length on his own Rabid, licensed out to dh2. Expect the polyrhythmic, tropics, adjacent club constructions he has been issuing in EP, sized doses for years, now stretched to album length.

title: Feeling Is Structure
description: New Max Cooper LP, the British producer continuing his run of cerebral, generative, leaning electronics where the maths and the melody pull in roughly the same direction. Worth a look if Yearning for the Infinite still gets played.

title: Train on the Island
label: 4AD Ltd
description: Aldous Harding back on 4AD, still operating in that unsettled folk, pop register where the vowels do half the work. The tag says alternative; in practice expect the same dry stagecraft as Designer and Warm Chris.

title: Duori
label: Stroom
description: Heith's Milan, circuit electronics meet Tarawangsawelas' two, string Sundanese bowing, landing on Stroom where this kind of cross, wired ritual music tends to find its natural shelf. Filed near Gabber Modus Operandi for anyone who wants the pointer.

title: Everybody Sensitive
description: Outside the usual remit for this site, but Kendrick rarely arrives without a producer roster worth scanning, and his post, GNX run has been closer to the rap mainstream's flirtation with electronic and West Coast funk textures than anything else in the charts.

title: Sol.Hz
label: Warp Records
description: Seefeel back on Warp, which is either a loaded proposition or exactly where they belong depending on how you feel about Quique and Succour still sounding like the future. Expect more of that rhythm, versus, drone tension they have always worked inside.

title: No One Plays The Game
label: 3024 Music
description: Martyn linking up with Duval Timothy on his own 3024, the Dutch broken, beat lifer meeting the London pianist in slowed, downtempo territory rather than on a dancefloor. For anyone who followed Voids further inward.

title: Ride TV
label: Smalltown Supersound
description: DJ Plead lands on Smalltown Supersound with three tracks pulling his percussion, forward club work toward dub and dancehall, with the edges blurred into ambient. Limited 12", shelve alongside Toma Kami if you need an angle.

title: THE WELFARE OF FORGOTTEN THINGS
label: Snowfall
description: Spoken, word alternative rap from Daragh Fleming over Throwing Snow's production, landing on the latter's Snowfall imprint. The pairing leans more towards the bass, weighted, clouded register Throwing Snow has worked in for years than anything resembling a straight rap single.

title: Jpap x coco
description: KOSMOS turns up with a one, off single, label unconfirmed, dropped without much in the way of context. File under watch, this, space until more surfaces.

title: Samsara Spirals
label: TOYS Berlin
description: Asa 808 links up with Throwing Snow on TOYS Berlin, two producers whose catalogues have long orbited broken, beat, bass, weighted electronica from different angles. A meeting of regulars rather than a crossover event.

title: SAGES (Echoes Edition)
label: A Mercury KX Release; Ólafur Arnalds, under exclusive license to Universal Music Operations Limited
description: Ólafur Arnalds pivots further into vocal, led territory, expanding the SAGES project with Loreen in tow for Mercury KX. Neoclassical scaffolding meets full, weight pop; closer to Island Songs scaled up than to anything on Erased Tapes.

title: Gravity
description: Noon returns with "Gravity," a single arriving without label or format confirmed as of writing. File alongside the rest of the catalogue until more surfaces.

title: ARORA
label: 11446626 Records DK
description: Rustie leaning into full trance register, the maximalist Glaswegian palette pointed at euphoric builds rather than rap production. Self, released via the DK distributor tag, so treat it as a direct drop.

title: Friend Remixes
label: AD 93
description: Remixes of material from James K's Friend, the NYC vocalist whose work sits at the hazier edge of dream pop and club music. No label or tracklist surfaced yet; worth a watch if Aya or Loraine James reworks are your thing.

title: E At Home
label: Shelter Press
description: Four short pieces from Eliana Glass on a limited 7", Shelter Press shelving jazz next to its usual diet of composition and poetics. Slight, parlour, scaled, more sketchbook than statement.

title: Singing
label: Jagjaguwar
description: Gia Margaret returns to voice, led songwriting on Jagjaguwar after the ambient detours, twelve tracks shelved more comfortably next to the label's folk roster than her piano sketchbooks. Quiet music that doesn't mistake itself for background.

title: Gravity
label: Zime Media AB
description: A NOON and fatbasso collaboration on Zime Media, filed simply under electronic. Worth a listen on the strength of the pairing alone.

title: V.O.E.M (feat. TWH)
description: Klein returns in her usual mode of sounding like nobody else, vocal, built collage that treats song form as suggestion. The TWH feature is the only fixed coordinate; expect the rest to drift past gospel, theatre and corrupted r&b on its own schedule.

title: THIS ONE A KEEPER
description: Matt Cutler back under the Lone alias, a producer whose lane has long been rave euphoria filtered through pastel, bright sample work. Label unconfirmed at time of writing; expect the usual Lone signatures rather than a swerve.

title: SAGES (Echoes Edition)
description: An expanded edition of the Icelandic composer's latest, extending his familiar territory of piano figures, processed strings and small electronic gestures. For listeners who have stayed with him since Found Songs.

title: 10000 Miles
description: Stefan Betke continues his long project of cracking, clicking dub electronics into something quieter and more architectural. For anyone who has stayed with the Pole catalogue past the colour trilogy.

title: Rosebush Pruning (Original Soundtrack Album)
label: Accidental Ltd
description: Herbert returns to film scoring on his own Accidental imprint, which, given his track record, usually means musique concrète impulses pressed into something more compositional. Worth watching for anyone who followed the Goodbye Swingtime lineage as much as the club work.

title: Orin
label: Latency
description: Villalobos meeting Koshiro Hino's goat on Latency is the kind of pairing the label was built for: Japanese percussive minimalism filtered through the Perlon regular's rhythmic drift. One to file alongside the Latency catalogue's more patient end.

title: i co potem?!?
description: Karuzelkaaa returns with a short piece whose details remain close to the chest, no label, no tags, just a title that shrugs its own question. Worth a listen on arrival before the context catches up.

title: Orin (Ricardo Villalobos Variation)
description: Villalobos in remix mode, which historically means a track gets stretched, hollowed out, and reassembled around its own negative space. Label details still pending; file alongside the rest of his long tail of variations.

title: Spring summer
label: Escho
description: Smerz return to Escho with another single in their oblique pop register, the production as exposed and unbothered as ever. Vocals up close, structures still refusing to behave.

title: Wasteman (Original Motion Picture Soundtrack)
label: Dense Truth
description: Forest Swords scores a feature, out via his own Dense Truth imprint. Expect the same corroded, ritual, feeling electronics that marked Compassion, arranged here for picture.

title: Out of Place
label: False Idols
description: Tricky pairs with Marta for a single on his own False Idols, the imprint that has housed most of his work since leaving the majors. Expect the murk and half, whispered vocal trade, offs he has been refining for three decades.

artist: Alan & Jan, Alan Abrahams & Jan Jelinek
title: All One
label: Faitiche
description: Alan Abrahams and Jan Jelinek pair up on Faitiche, which usually means patient, process, led electronics with the edges left audible. For anyone who followed Jelinek's Loop, finding, Jazz, Records into its quieter offshoots.

title: Eusexua Afterglow
label: Young (5)
description: Eleven tracks extending the Eusexua project further into dance, pop territory, with Twigs still threading her usual art, school physicality through club shapes. Young keeps releasing it as pop that refuses to quite behave as such.

title: Out of Place
description: Tricky returns with a new single, the Bristol veteran still working the same smoked, paranoid trip, hop register he essentially defined. Whispered menace remains the default mode.

title: All One
description: Jelinek in single form, which historically means a small idea worried over until it dissolves into its own grain. File alongside the Faitiche catalogue and expect more questions than statements.

title: GroakDontCroak vol. 1
description: Xang opens a numbered series under a title that already reads like a private joke, with no label or tracklist surfaced yet. One to file away and revisit when the rest of the picture arrives.

title: GroakDontCroak vol. 1 [Explicit]
description: Xang collects a first volume under the GroakDontCroak banner, self, released and arriving with no label scaffolding to lean on. Worth approaching cold.

title: Barrons Hotel / Yellow Bones
label: Fixed Abode
description: Purelink's ambient dub meets Rainy Miller's bruised, post, everything songcraft on Fixed Abode, a pairing that makes more sense the longer you sit with either catalogue. For anyone who rinsed Signs or Desquite.

title: Zur زور
label: Other People, distributed by Stem
description: Peyghamy's tombak, driven electronics land on Other People, where his patient, percussion, first approach fits neatly alongside the label's long, running interest in acoustic, electronic hybrids. For anyone tracking the Nicolas Jaar orbit.

title: Barrons Hotel/Yellow Bones
description: Purelink return to the long, form, the Chicago trio still working that patient ambient, dub register where house architecture dissolves into vapor. For anyone tracking the lineage from Pole through Huerco S.

title: Donna EP
description: Wolfgang Voigt back under the GAS alias, where the format reads "EP" but the working method, classical loops dissolved into forest, floor 4/4, rarely arrives in short forms. File alongside the Kompakt continuum and wait for the pressing details.

title: Kill Switch
description: Ital Tek in single form, where his usual register sits somewhere between cinematic bass weight and the more fractured end of Planet Mu's catalogue. Worth a listen if Outland still holds your attention.

title: Masduros
description: PPP returns with a single titled Masduros, label unconfirmed at time of writing. File alongside the rest of the project's catalogue and judge it on arrival.

title: Barrons Hotel/Yellow Bones
description: Rainy Miller in his usual mode: bleached northern emo, rap and torch, song production, the Preston dialect threaded through digital decay. For anyone tracking the Fixed Abode orbit.

title: Better
description: New Baauer single, arriving without label info or much of a paper trail. Expect the trap, adjacent club instincts he's been trading in since Harlem Shake hardened into a working method.

title: Stoner Olympics
description: Eyedress in his usual lane of hazy, lo, fi bedroom pop with a slacker, rap tilt, arriving on a 4/20 release date that telegraphs its mood clearly enough. For anyone still pulling Mulholland Drive off the shelf.

title: i never had a chance at heaven in the first place, lets blaze this spliff
description: KOSMOS turns up self, released with a title that already tells you the mood. Take it as stoner, room ambient until proven otherwise.

title: MASSACRE
description: Pessimist working in the register he's known for, that grim, percussive variant of drum and bass where the breaks feel weighted rather than propulsive. Title suggests no softening of approach.

title: As Time Explodes (Live Album)
label: Reprise Records
description: A thirteen, track live document from Young and his current band, issued for Record Store Day in a limited edition on Reprise. Not electronic, but included for the archivists.

title: Sound Mirrors
label: Ninja Tune
description: Ninja Tune bosses return to the long, player format for Record Store Day, twelve tracks stretching across breaks, downtempo, deep house and future jazz. A wide remit handled by people who have spent decades working exactly this territory.

title: Live At Metropolis
label: Ninja Tune
description: A six, track Metropolis session pressed for Record Store Day, catching Yanya's indie rock in a room, sounding document for Ninja Tune.

title: MindsEye
label: Erased Tapes Records
description: Rival Consoles heads to the screen for Erased Tapes, ten tracks pulling his techno instincts toward something harsher and more industrial. Pressed at 45 RPM across a limited 12", with soundtrack duties shaping the edges.

title: Sledgehammer
label: Real World Records
description: A Record Store Day picture disc reissue of the 1986 hit, returned to wax via Real World in a limited 45 RPM 12" pressing. Three tracks for the collectors' shelf rather than the curious newcomer.

label: Plug Research
description: Remastered reissue of the Flying Lotus debut for Record Store Day, ten tracks sitting at the intersection of IDM, downtempo and nascent future jazz that would define the Brainfeeder house style.

title: AGATE
label: Kitchen. Label
description: Seven pieces of ambient electronics from Meitei, arriving on Kitchen. Label in a limited LP pressing. Shelve near Chihei Hatakeyama if you need a pointer.

title: 478 freestyle (feat. Celeste)
description: A new Dean Blunt single with Celeste on the mic, the title doing its usual job of telling you almost nothing.

title: life of mu
description: A full length from mu tate arriving in April, with label, genre and tracklist all still undisclosed. Worth flagging now and circling back once more of it surfaces.

title: Epoch
label: Ghostly International
description: Limited repress of the Ghostly ambient/chillwave set across eleven tracks, returning to vinyl in April 2026 for those who missed the original run.

title: Relentless Opponent
label: Throttle Records Ltd
description: Clark forwards a single on his own Throttle imprint, IDM and techno filtered through the granular, almost orchestral density he has leaned into since Death Peak. Digital only for now.

title: Palestine 36
label: Invada Records
description: Frost scoring a period film for Invada, eight cues leaning on the industrial and noise textures he has pushed through A U R O R A and his Lynch work. Shelve near Tim Hecker's soundtrack output if you need a pointer.

title: Echoes
label: A Mercury KX Release; Ólafur Arnalds, under exclusive license to Universal Music Operations Limited
description: Ólafur Arnalds lends his string, and, piano palette to a Mercury KX pop single fronted by Loreen and SAGES, the neoclassical vocabulary repurposed as scaffolding for a large, format vocal. For listeners who followed Arnalds' Island Songs crossover work more than the ambient sides.

title: Superbloom
label: EMI
description: Ware continues down the mirrorball path she has been working since What's Your Pleasure?, thirteen tracks of nu, disco and dance, pop for EMI. Shelve alongside Roisin Murphy if the Hot Chip crowd needs a pointer.

title: Night , Blooming Jasmine .
description: A self, released single from fakemink, surfacing with no label and no tagging to anchor it. File it among the loose digital one, offs you find by following the artist rather than the shelf.

title: Till Your Mind Is Shining (Bright-Side Mix)
label: Real World Records
description: Gabriel's Real World operation keeps feeding the post, i/o catalogue with alternate mixes, this one a brightened pass at a song that sits firmly in his art, rock lane. One track, studio polish intact, for completists already deep in the Bright, Side sequence.

title: Malibu
label: OBE
description: The soul, rap record that broke Anderson .Paak into wider view, sixteen tracks threading live drums, gospel warmth and west coast swing. A decade on it still sits comfortably next to Kaytranada or early Thundercat if you need a shelf.

title: Malibu = 말리부
label: OBE
description: A Korean picture disc reissue of Anderson .Paak's 2016 breakthrough, sixteen tracks of California neo, soul, loose, limbed funk and rapped, sung confession that established the voice he has spent the decade since trying to outrun. Numbered edition via OBE.

title: Otro Perro A Ese Hueso
description: Klein back in her own orbit, which has always meant sacred music, R&B and tape, damaged sound design colliding without warning. Expect nothing settled; she rarely offers it.

title: burn quik (shubz mix)
description: A shubz mix of burn quik from Klein, who has spent the last several years turning R&B, choral fragments and sound design into something closer to theatre than song. Self, released, as her work tends to be.

title: Feels Good EP
label: Cécille Numbers
description: Two tracks of functional, peak, time tech house from the Bambossa veteran, landing on Cécille's digital sub, label. Built for the room rather than the headphones.

title: Look At Yourself
label: Synkro Musik
description: Two tracks from Synkro on Mindset, splitting the difference between juke's footwork pulse and the more reflective end of his techno work. Cut at variable speeds, which tells you most of what you need to know about how it's meant to be played.

title: 478 freestyle
description: Another Dean Blunt full, length arriving with the usual lack of context, title and date and not much else. Expect the customary fog of guitar, strings, and sub, bass arranged with deliberate refusal; Blunt remains his own genre.

title: Les Sirènes
description: Laurel Halo returns to the long, form, several years on from Atlas, with the abstract chamber, electronic palette she has been working in since leaving the club behind. Details still thin, but the company she keeps suggests Awe rather than Quarantine.

title: HOTLIFE [Explicit]
description: Tiga returns to long, format with HOTLIFE, the Montreal vocalist, producer still operating in the arch, deadpan electro, house register he has worked since Sunglasses At Night. File alongside Jacques Lu Cont if you need a shelving cue.

title: I Carry the Strength
description: Słyż continues her work in computer music and spatialised electronics, a register she has built across festival commissions and Polish experimental circles. Title and date are about all that's confirmed; expect texture over melody.

title: Echoes
description: Another single from the Icelandic composer whose neo, classical piano and processed strings have become a fixture of the post, Jóhannsson landscape. Expect restraint rather than reinvention.

title: HOTLIFE
label: Secret City Records
description: Tiga lands on Secret City with twelve tracks of house and techno cut for the floor rather than the lounge. The Turbo boss working in his usual register: arch, vocal, led, built for prime time.

title: Earth A God
description: New Jlin album incoming for spring, the Gary, Indiana producer continuing the percussive logic that took footwork somewhere it had never been asked to go. File next to Halcyon Veil and the more rhythm, forward end of Planet Mu.

title: GUERILLAZ
description: A collaborative single from H.LLS and Lucy Park, slated for April 2026.

title: Boots on the Ground
label: Play It Again Sam
description: Massive Attack break a long silence with a single for PIAS, landing in the same low, lit trip hop register Bristol built its reputation on. One track, digital only, weight implied in the title.

title: LEPSZE DNI NAD PL
description: Karuzelkaaa continues in the lane of Polish internet, native pop that has been quietly building its own grammar, somewhere between bedroom rap, cloud, adjacent production and post, SoundCloud melancholy. File with the younger end of the Warsaw underground.

title: GUERILLAZ
description: H.LLS returns with a full, length called GUERILLAZ, the title doing most of the talking before a single track plays. Worth a listen for anyone tracking the harder, more confrontational fringes of club music.

title: No Volume Limit
description: Andrea returns to long, form, the Ilian Tape regular whose records have always sat between rave memory and something more pensive. Worth checking if Due in Colour stayed in your rotation.

title: Intarsia
description: New short, form work from the Portland duo whose patchwork of MIDI, synthesis software and fourth, world reference points has shaped a particular corner of post, Hosono ambient. File alongside Yoshio Ojima or Motion Graphics.

title: LUX (Complete Works)
label: Columbia
description: Columbia consolidates the LUX material into an eighteen, track edition that pulls Rosalía's flamenco, classical instincts further from anything recognisable as pop radio. The orchestral writing keeps the centre of gravity; the production stays restless around it.

title: Heavy Sound
description: A single broken, beat cut on Martyn's own 3024, leaning into the breaks and future jazz end of the catalogue. Self, released house business for anyone still working through the label's back pages.

title: Blinkmoth (July Mix) (Special Guest DJ VIP)
description: A James K single arriving with a remix credit baked into the title, pointing to the Special Guest DJ orbit she has kept close to for years. Expect the bleary, vocal, forward dream, pop register her Incienso sides have mapped out.

title: Doom Bikini (Hesaitix Remix)
description: Hesaitix takes a scalpel to a James K track, which on paper alone is enough to warrant attention: her fogged, vocal, forward dream, pop rewired by one of the more slippery producers in the current West Mineral orbit.

title: Come Unprepared
description: New Plaid album landing in spring, presumably keeping to the melodic, fastidiously arranged IDM the duo have been refining since the Black Dog days. Treat as Warp, adjacent listening until the tracklist surfaces.

title: Insane Y triste
description: Lone surfaces with a new long, player, label undisclosed for now, presumably more of the rave, tinted, sun, warm production he has built a catalogue on since Galaxy Garden. Worth flagging early for anyone who never quite got over Reality Testing.

title: Blinkmoth (July Mix) (Special Guest DJ VIP)
description: Special Guest DJ revisits Blinkmoth in VIP form, the project's tendency toward woozy, club, adjacent edits intact. Self, released and unceremonious, as these things tend to be.

title: Silently
label: World of Echo
description: Bristol's Tara Clerkin Trio return to World of Echo, where their hushed, jazz, adjacent songform tends to sit closest to the room itself. For listeners already deep in the In Camera EP.

title: Blue Kembang
label: Stroom
description: Heith's metallic, ritual, leaning electronics meet Tarawangsawelas' Sundanese two, string drone on Stroom, a pairing that makes more sense the longer you sit with it. For anyone following Ghédalia Tazartès reissues or the stranger corners of the label's catalogue.

title: Blue Kembang
description: Heith back in single form, which usually means another angle on the smoke, and, percussion ritualism he has been mapping out since Hallmark of Ghost. Worth a listen if PAN's more occult end still pulls you in.

title: Oracles
label: Local Action Records
description: Five tracks from Om Unit on Local Action, pulling his long, running fascinations with breaks, dub weight and soundsystem pressure into something closer to a club EP than a meditation. For anyone who kept hold of Threads.

title: Dirty Shore Town
description: New long, player from Malibu, whose foggy, choral ambient, pop has drifted further from club logic with each release. File alongside Croatian Amor if you need a shelf.

title: Flatline
description: Loraine James in single mode, where her usual fractured drum programming and quiet emotional weight tend to land in their most concentrated form. One to file alongside her Hyperdub catalogue.

title: Lonesome For A Storm
label: Motion Ward
description: Fifteen folk pieces from Gustav Kemps, filed under Motion Ward, a label more often associated with ambient and club edges than acoustic songform. The incongruity is likely the point.

title: Everything U
description: DJ Seinfeld continues mining the lovelorn end of house music, where filtered chords and softened drum machines double as a mood ring. Same emotional register as the Mirrors, era material, for anyone who never quite left it behind.

title: SpaceBoy
description: Scott Monteith back under the Deadbeat alias, where the brief has long been dub techno played slow enough to hear the room. Label unannounced for now, but the register is unlikely to surprise anyone still spinning Something Borrowed, Something Blue.

title: Kammerkonzert
label: Warp Records
description: Squarepusher returns to Warp with a fifteen, track set that leans further into the jazz end of his catalogue, framed as chamber music rather than club fare. Experimental enough to reward close listening, familiar enough for anyone who has followed the Warp lineage.

title: Architectonics
label: Peak Oil
description: Eleven pieces from hoavi for Peak Oil, threading gamelan textures through dub techno haze and abstract ambient drift. Quiet company for anyone still playing Topdown Dialectic.

title: In Filth Your Mystery Is Kingdom / Far-Smile Peasant In Yellow Music
label: AD 93
description: Fourteen tracks for AD 93 that sit awkwardly between folk song and electronic abstraction, its lo, fi psychedelia frayed enough to feel half, remembered. For listeners drawn to the stranger corners of the label's roster.

title: Polytoxicomane De Toi
label: Pan European Recording
description: Six tracks of French darkwave on Pan European, pitched somewhere between pop gesture and nocturnal sulk. Recommended if the gloomier corners of the label's roster are already on your shelf.

title: Who Cares?
label: Purely Physical Teeny Tapes
description: Self, titled EP from Who Cares?, arriving on Purely Physical Teeny Tapes in April 2026. Minimal metadata, which feels appropriate to the name.

title: Seismo
label: Pan (3)
description: An eight, track collaboration on PAN pairing Upsammy's electronics with Valentina Magaletti's percussion, filed somewhere between experimental electronics and free jazz.

artist: PPP, Piezo, Dj Plead & DJ Python
title: Bborn Again
label: Wisdom Teeth
description: Four, way split on Wisdom Teeth pairing PPP and Piezo with DJ Plead and DJ Python, a roster that suggests the EP sits somewhere between club tools and the weirder end of the label's catalogue.

title: Seismo
label: PAN
description: Eight tracks of electronics and percussion meeting somewhere between experimental composition and free jazz, landing on Pan next April. An unusually open setting for both players.

title: Reflections Vol. 3: Water Poems
label: RVNG Intl.
description: Eight ambient pieces from two artists whose individual catalogs have long orbited this kind of patient, close, listening work. RVNG continues its Reflections series into its third volume.

title: Whatever You Do
label: Sony Music Entertainment Germany GmbH
description: The Belgian techno mainstay turns up on Sony Germany rather than her usual Lenske channel, a single built for the kind of peak, time functionality her sets have always traded in. File next to Charlotte de Witte if you need a coordinate.

title: Hyperphantasia
label: Greco-Roman
description: Lone returns to Greco, Roman with sixteen tracks spread across the full Magicwire palette: rave, era breaks, warm house, downtempo and ambient smudges all accounted for. Maximalist as ever, and shelved somewhere between Bibio and his own Galaxy Garden.

title: Flow Free
label: Future Classic
description: Panama and Christian Löffler meet on Future Classic, which on paper reads like a neat alignment of the label's smoother Australian end and Löffler's forest, ambient house. File alongside Ben Böhmer.

title: Bborn Again
description: New one from DJ Plead, still working that lopsided edge where club percussion and MENA rhythmic cues rub against each other without settling. For anyone who stuck with the Nervous Horizon material.

artist: Squarepusher = スクエアプッシャー
title: Kammerkonzert = カンマーコンツェルト
label: Warp Records
description: Tom Jenkinson's long tenure on Warp continues with a fourteen, track set that leans audibly toward the jazz side of his ledger, experimental in the composerly sense the title implies. Limited LP pressing for those who file him next to Autechre.

title: My Favorite Things
label: Atlantic
description: Atlantic return to the 1961 modal landmark where Coltrane rerouted a show tune into a vehicle for soprano saxophone and McCoy Tyner's suspended chords. Four tracks, reissue pressing; foundational listening that doesn't need defending.

title: parl cu me
description: K, LONE steps out from Wisdom Teeth with a single whose label is, for now, undisclosed. Expect the same soft, focus take on UK club music, percussive but rarely insistent, that has defined his recent twelves.

title: Maybe Not Tonight
label: So Young Records
description: Second Lime Garden LP for So Young, ten tracks of the Brighton quartet's guitar, forward alt, pop in a numbered limited pressing. Shelve near Dry Cleaning if you need a pointer, though the register here is warmer.

title: Nausea
label: FELT (3)
description: Seven pieces of unsettled ambient and drone from Grady Steele, issued by FELT as a mini, album. Closer to seasick than meditative, with the queasiness the title suggests left intact.

title: vernacular
label: life is beautiful records
description: Seven tracks from Aloisius that sit uneasily between rock instrumentation, classical phrasing, and electronic processing, issued on LP by life is beautiful records. Experimental without theatrics, closer to a working document than a finished statement.

title: Idea 1
label: Warp Records
description: Kelela on Warp, leaning into shoegaze territory rather than the club, adjacent R&B she is usually filed under. A single track, so treat it as a sketch rather than a statement.

title: In Reverse (Polygonia Remix)
label: Erased Tapes Records Ltd.
description: Polygonia takes the Rival Consoles track into her own percussive, tunnelling register, trading Ryan Lee West's melodic patience for something closer to the Munich techno end of things. Still on Erased Tapes, but pointed at the dancefloor.

title: Plastic Camelia / Laurel
label: Rabid Records under exclusive license to dh2
description: One half of The Knife back on Rabid, licensed through dh2, with two tracks that sit in the bright, percussive corner of his solo work rather than the sibling, project pop. For anyone who played the Coral cuts into the ground.

title: Exercicis Ritmics Volum 2
label: Hivern Discs
description: Five tracks of rhythm studies from Oma Totem, landing on Hivern Discs where bass weight, dubstep pressure and techno structure tend to overlap without apology. Shelves near Pugilist or the harder end of the John Talabot extended family.

title: Selected Ambient Works 85-92
label: Apollo
description: Apollo reissues the Aphex Twin catalogue anchor across thirteen tracks, still sitting somewhere between ambient, techno and electro without fully committing to any of them. The pressing returns to LP for anyone who wore through the last copy.

title: Τι Κι Αν Δεν Είσαι Ήρωας
label: Heaven OST
description: A soundtrack single from Idra Kayne and Christos Alexopoulos for the Heaven OST imprint, filed under stage and screen rather than club use. Greek, language vocal writing set against orchestrated cues, best approached as part of the picture it was made for.

title: walking shoe
label: ost euro
description: Four tracks from Kvisha on Ost Euro, splitting the difference between functional minimal techno and the fussier bleep, and, click end of IDM. A 12" for anyone who still files Minus next to Skam.

title: Untitled
label: Warp Records
description: A one, track, NTSC, format ambient collage issued through Warp, the physical medium itself already half the statement. Untitled in every sense, and best approached that way.

title: Volumes:  One - Selections From Music Concerts 2019-2023 Bon Iver 6 Piece Band (Japan Edition)
label: Jagjaguwar
description: A Japan edition live document drawing from Bon Iver's six, piece band performances across 2019 to 2023, collected across eleven tracks on limited LP via Jagjaguwar.

title: Distracted
label: Brainfeeder
description: Fifteen tracks of Thundercat on Brainfeeder, still working the seam where jazz bass, funk, and hip hop overlap. One for anyone who has been paying attention since Drunk.

title: Dark Sky Reservation
label: Real World Records
description: Fourteen tracks on Real World that sit between electronic, classical and folk gestures without fully committing to any of them. Experimental in temperament rather than texture, which suits the label's long, standing catalogue.

title: Pompeii/Utility
label: 10K
description: Thirty, three tracks across a joint LP from Mike, Surf Gang and Earl Sweatshirt, landing on 10K in spring 2026. A lot to sit with.

title: Volumes: One - Selections From Music Concerts 2019-2023 Bon Iver 6 Piece Band
label: Jagjaguwar
description: Eleven, track live compilation drawn from the six, piece band configuration across a four, year touring window, arriving on Jagjaguwar in the spring. Closer to a working document than a greatest, hits, with the electronic and art, rock edges of the catalogue presumably sharpened by the road.

title: Volumes One (Selections From Music Concerts 2019-2023 Bon Iver 6 Piece Band)
label: Jagjaguwar
description: Eleven selections drawn from the 2019, 2023 six, piece live run, collected by Jagjaguwar as a limited stereo LP. Folk frames stretched out into something looser and band, shaped rather than studio, bound.

title: NUKU
label: Nyege Nyege Tapes
description: Two, track collaboration on Nyege Nyege Tapes, pitched between E'DU and Judgitzu's takes on contemporary African club music. For anyone already following the Kampala label's output.

title: Nuku
label: Nyege Nyege Tapes
description: Two tracks of E'DU and Judgitzu trading ideas on Nyege Nyege Tapes, filed under African electronics. A short, functional release for anyone already tracking the Kampala label's output.

title: Ambiguous Desire
label: Transgressive Records
description: Twelve tracks of indie pop on Transgressive, issued as a limited LP. Parks stays in the confessional register her name is built on, filed here mostly for listeners already tracking her.

artist: Nightmares On Wax VS Adrian Sherwood = ナイトメアズ・オン・ワックス* VS エイドリアン・シャーウッド
title: In A Space Outta Dub = イン・ア・スペース・アウタ・ダブ
label: Warp Records
description: Sherwood takes the faders to a Nightmares On Wax record, eight tracks of downtempo and trip hop refracted through dub on Warp. Limited LP pressing due next April.

title: Till Your Mind Is Shining (Dark-Side Mix)
label: Real World Records
description: A remix cut from the Real World camp, Gabriel's songcraft pulled toward its shadowed edge rather than its widescreen one. One track, sequenced for late listening rather than radio.

title: Ebb And Flow
description: New single from Max Cooper. Beyond that the metadata is thin, so take this as a placeholder rather than a verdict.

title: Lateral
label: Short Span
description: Twelve tracks of ambient, minimal and dub techno on Short Span, where Mammo leans into the quieter end of the spectrum without abandoning the pulse underneath.

title: Chainsaw Man The Movie: Reze Arc Original Soundtrack - Summer's End -
label: Mappa Records
description: Thirty cues from Kensuke Ushio for the Reze Arc film, pressed to LP in mixed stereo and mono by Mappa Records themselves. A score album aimed at listeners who followed Ushio's work on the series proper.

title: The Yall Street Journal Extra Extra Vol.1
label: Brown Records
description: Band Of Horses turn up on Brown Records with a five, track 10" that sits squarely in their folk rock and indie rock lane. Club edition pressing for anyone still keeping shelf space for the band.

title: The III Hands Of Doom
label: Nyege Nyege Tapes
description: A three, way meeting on Nyege Nyege Tapes, with four tracks pulling Afrobeat rhythm work through dub techno weight. Worth a look if the label's recent output has been holding your attention.

title: Silent Way
label: Plastic & Sounds
description: The famously reclusive Chain Reaction alumnus resurfaces with another studio of glassy, narcotic dub techno. Loops drift rather than lock; for anyone still returning to Butterfly Effects.

title: Sexistential
label: Young (5)
description: Nine tracks of dance, pop on Young, issued as a limited LP. The kind of record Robyn makes when she decides to make one.

title: Kissing Luck Goodbye
label: Dais Records
description: Twelve tracks of electro, EBM and synthpunk from ADULT., landing on Dais in a limited LP pressing. Abrasive terrain for anyone still keeping tabs on Boy Harsher or the wider Dais roster.

title: Ö
label: Ninja Tune
description: Fcukers land on Ninja Tune with eleven tracks of electro house shaded by electroclash instincts, a record that seems built for the hour when the room tips from dancing into something messier.

title: Nocturnal Consolations
label: Instant Classic
description: A duo record for Instant Classic, eleven tracks stretched across an LP that sits closer to folk than to the label's usual leftfield fare. Worth a listen if Rogiński's prior work on the label holds your attention.

title: Home Safe
label: Erased Tapes Records
description: Eleven tracks from Crayon for Erased Tapes, sitting somewhere between electro, hip hop and pop without settling on any of them. A limited LP pressing for March.

title: High Cube
label: Geographic North
description: Six tracks of ambient, experimental techno from the Foote/Dickow pairing, landing on Atlanta's Geographic North in a limited 12" pressing. Closer to the label's patient, zoned, out end than its dancefloor side.

title: Kinshasa In Action
label: Nyege Nyege Tapes
description: Eleven tracks of Kinshasa street noise, scrap, metal percussion and Afrobeat rhythm pushed into the red, exactly the kind of document Nyege Nyege Tapes exists to issue. For anyone shelving Jako Maron near their field, recording LPs.

title: Moo, You Bloody Choir
label: Sony Music
description: Augie March's widescreen literary indie rock gets another Columbia pressing, fourteen tracks of the wordy, melodically overgrown songwriting the band has traded in for two decades. Shelve with the Go, Betweens if you need a pointer.

title: The Whole Truth
label: R & S Records
description: Single, track drum and bass outing for R & S, the kind of catalogue entry the label has been steadily expanding into alongside its techno spine. Functional rather than showy, aimed at the floor.

title: Dim Stars / For Residue (Extended)
label: Warp Records
description: Two long-form Lopatin sketches extended into the kind of elastic, synth-warped ambient he has been quietly refining since Magic Oneohtrix. Warp doing what Warp does.

title: Bursting Dementia
label: Into It Records
description: Ten tracks of technical death metal with thrash bones, reissued through Into It Records. Shelve near the mid, period Death and Atheist end of the shelf if you need bearings.

title: GEKO01
label: GEKO
description: Melbourne duo inaugurate their own GEKO label with four cuts of live-edit dub, broken beat and reverb-soaked house. Built from jam sessions, left rough on purpose.

title: The Moth
label: Motion Ward
description: Six tracks of smudged neofolk and post, rock debris from Cancer House, landing on Motion Ward in a limited LP run. Closer to a tape, warped song cycle than an ambient record, though the dark, ambient haze is doing plenty of the structural work.

title: Chapter II
label: Good Morning Tapes
description: Six dub workouts on Good Morning Tapes, where the label's incense, and, cassette ambient remit stretches sideways into bass weight. Sits comfortably alongside the slower Seekersinternational material if you need a shelving cue.

title: Black Sands
label: Ninja Tune
description: Ninja Tune wheels out a fresh pressing of the 2010 Bonobo LP, still the cleanest articulation of his orchestral, leaning downtempo before the rooms got bigger. Sits comfortably next to Cinematic Orchestra on the shelf.

title: Hinterlands
label: Ghostly International
description: Green, House lands on Ghostly with twelve pieces of the gentle, plant, facing ambient she has built her catalogue around. Sits comfortably next to Ana Roxanne if you need a shelving cue.

title: Ode To Final Fantasy
label: Erased Tapes Records
description: Eleven pieces of ambient folk on Erased Tapes built around the Final Fantasy songbook, the source material treated as standards rather than nostalgia bait. For anyone who plays Nils Frahm and Hatis Noit at the same volume.

title: Spandrel?
label: Pan (3)
description: PAN reissues Evita Manji's grief, processing record on vinyl, ten pieces of brittle digital ambient and processed voice that sit closer to ruin than to club. For anyone tracking the label's Sky H1 axis.

title: Everything All The Time
label: Sub Pop
description: Sub Pop runs the reissue press again on the 2006 Band Of Horses debut, the one that turned Ben Bridwell's reverb, heavy holler into a small festival currency for the rest of the decade. Padded out to nineteen tracks for the LP edition.

title: Bongo Fury (50th Anniversary Edition)
label: UMe
description: Half, century reissue of the 1975 Zappa and Beefheart live document, remastered and bulked out to 78 tracks of stage banter, alternates and rehearsal scraps. Strictly for the deep, catalogue shelf, not the entry point.

title: Applications II
label: Ilian Tape
description: Four tracks of Shed on Ilian Tape, which lines up about as neatly as a techno release can in 2026. Expect the rugged, slightly broken, stepping end of his catalogue rather than straight 4/4; shelve next to the Zenker Brothers.

title: AKA SYT
label: Grabaciones Bonicas
description: Fourteen tracks of scrappy post, punk on Barcelona's Grabaciones Bonicas, leaning more new wave nerve than hardcore homage despite the name. Shelve near the label's other guitar, forward outliers.

title: Letters./Hung Up on a Line
label: Fixed Abode
description: A two, sided collaboration on Fixed Abode, with Berzigotti and Allen working the seam where dream pop frays into something more experimental. Vocals as texture more than hook.

title: What Lies Ahead (Dark-Side Mix)
label: Real World Records
description: A Dark, Side mix of "What Lies Ahead" arrives on Real World as a stereo FLAC single, Gabriel continuing the alternate, perspective remix practice that ran through i/o. For listeners who treat his late, period output as one long, slowly turning piece.

title: Rust
label: Young And Cold Records
description: Ten tracks of post, punk leaning into goth rock and darkwave, due on Young And Cold next March. Cold guitars and drum, machine drive in the lineage the label has been quietly reinforcing for years.

title: The Smashing Machine
label: Warp Records
description: Sinephro scores Benny Safdie's wrestling drama for Warp, eight pieces extending the harp, and, modular calm of Endlessness into picture work. The pedal, steel ambient crowd will follow her here without complaint.

title: II
label: Peak Oil
description: Seven tracks of abstracted IDM and ambient drift on Peak Oil, the LA imprint quietly building a catalogue of after, hours electronics. Sits comfortably alongside Pendant or Topdown Dialectic if you need a shelving cue.

title: Transmitter
label: Jagjaguwar
description: Max Clarke's Cut Worms project lands on Jagjaguwar with ten more songs in his AM, radio, Everly, leaning songbook mode. Limited LP pressing for those filing alongside Andy Shauf or Hamilton Leithauser.

title: In The Big Room
label: Real World Records
description: Fourteen tracks of Gabriel on his own Real World imprint, sitting where his art, rock instincts have always sat: ornate, studio, deep, occasionally brushing against downtempo electronics. For listeners who still reach for Up more than So.

title: World Of Trance 20 (Extended Mixes)
label: ZYX Music
description: Talla 2XLC's long, running uplifting, trance compendium reaches its twentieth installment on ZYX, this time in extended, mix form across eight tracks. Strictly for the hands, in, the, air faithful; shelve next to your Armada and Black Hole stacks.

artist: Nightmares On Wax vs Adrian Sherwood
title: In A Space Outta Dub
label: Warp Records
description: Sherwood takes the controls to Nightmares On Wax material, running the downtempo catalogue through On, U Sound's mixing, desk physics. Warp leaning into its trip hop lineage, with the dub engineer who actually built that sound at the faders.

title: Die Cry Hate
label: Young And Cold Records
description: Seven tracks of darkwave and goth, leaning post, punk reissued through Young And Cold, the Augsburg label that has been quietly mapping this corner of the synth, pop continuum for years. For shelves where Lebanon Hanover already lives.

title: glob
label: NAFF
description: Five tracks of microhouse threaded with dub techno haze on NAFF, the kind of record that rewards a louder system than you think it needs. For anyone keeping tabs on the label's quieter end.

title: Looking For Mount Sylvan
label: 12th Isle
description: A collaborative LP for 12th Isle, eight tracks of pastoral ambient and downtempo drift in keeping with Sarid's gentler new, age leanings and the label's wider Glasgow, via, elsewhere catalogue. For anyone who reaches for Ulla when the weather turns.

title: Sabine
label: Knekelhuis
description: Knekelhuis pulls Eye's Sabine back into print, eight tracks of cold synth, pop tilting into minimal techno that fit the label's ongoing excavation of post, punk era electronics. Remastered for this repress; sits comfortably next to Mark Du Mosch.

title: Big Mama
label: Brainfeeder
description: Ellison back on his own label with a single, sided 12", seven sketches that read more like a notebook dump than a proper EP: abstract beat work shaded with future, jazz harmony and the occasional chiptune squelch. Brainfeeder housekeeping, but the good kind.

title: Another/Weird Dream
label: Modern Love
description: A two, track 7" from MJ Guider on Modern Love, the New Orleans producer's blurred shoegaze, into, dub register pressed to its smallest possible format. Sits comfortably next to Grouper on the shelf.

title: Celliacus
label: Ramble Records
description: Seven tracks of free jazz and tape, edge experimentalism from Celliacus, landing on Ramble Records, the Melbourne imprint that has quietly built a catalogue around the unruly edges of improvised music. One for the Astral Spirits shelf.

title: Marble Sins
label: Wild Youth Digital
description: Ten tracks of post, punk shading into psych on Wild Youth Digital, the kind of record that wears its alternative, rock bones openly rather than hiding them under effects. Stereo LP for those who still want the object.

title: GÍria
label: Pan (3)
description: Five tracks for PAN that sit at the intersection the label has been working lately, where experimental electronics, hip hop cadence and a residue of soul rub against each other. Worth a look if Eartheater or Coby Sey holds your attention.

title: Basic Inventory
label: Opal Tapes
description: Nine tracks of grit and corroded noise from Xorgett, landing on Opal Tapes where this kind of industrial murk has always made sense. File next to Karen Gwyer's harsher excursions on the same imprint.

title: Ever No Way
label: Warp Records
description: Seefeel back on Warp with a single track in their long, running ambient dub register, the kind of slow, erosion textures they have been working since Quique. For anyone still pulling out Pole or early Chain Reaction sides.

title: The Family EP
label: Apollo
description: Three tracks from the long, running London techno fixture, landing on Apollo and split between the harder and more ambient ends of his register. R&S' ambient sublabel remains a sensible home for it.

title: Who Do We Think We Are = 紫の肖像
label: Warner Records
description: Warner reissues the 1973 Mk II swansong, the one cut in road, fatigued circumstances and usually filed below Machine Head in the canon. Worth revisiting for the grooves rather than the legend; "Woman From Tokyo" still does most of the heavy lifting.

title: Women And Children First = 暗黒の掟
label: Warner Records
description: Warner reissues the 1980 Van Halen LP in its Japanese sleeve, remastered across nine tracks. The one where the band started loosening the pop, metal template Roth and Eddie had built, leaning harder into swagger and sludge.

title: Detached From The Rest Of You
description: Loraine James returns to album length, presumably still threading her restless take on broken club rhythms, IDM and bruised vocal, led electronics. Whatever the home this time, the writing tends to feel like notebooks more than statements.

title: What Lies Ahead (Bright-Side Mix)
label: Real World Records
description: A single track from Gabriel's ongoing trickle of "Bright, Side" mixes on Real World, mid, tempo and orchestrally cushioned in the manner he has favoured since i/o. For listeners already inside that world rather than anyone looking for a way in.

title: Visions Of The Past
label: Apollo
description: Apollo dusts off Leiner's mid, 90s Swedish ambient, trance for a remastered LP pressing, ten tracks of long, corridor synth work that sit comfortably alongside the label's Biosphere and Locust catalogue. One for the R&S ambient shelf.

title: Premonitions
label: Young And Cold Records
description: Four tracks of darkwave and goth, leaning synth, pop reissued through Young And Cold, the German label that has spent the last decade quietly mapping this exact corner. Sits comfortably next to the Selofan end of the roster.

title: The Acrobat
label: Dais Records
description: Dais reissues the Death Of Lovers LP, eight tracks of widescreen post, punk that has always sat closer to shoegaze haze than to gothic austerity. For anyone whose Nothing and Whirr shelves are already in order.

title: Mama Said
label: Virgin America (2)
description: Reissue of Kravitz's 1991 second album, fourteen tracks of soul, leaning rock that leaned harder into the heartbreak register than the debut. Virgin America back catalogue, for anyone who still files Are You Gonna Go My Way next to Bill Withers.

title: Cheek To Cheek
label: Streamline Records (3)
description: Streamline puts the Bennett/Gaga standards collaboration back on wax for Record Store Day, nineteen tracks of straight, down, the, middle big, band jazz vocal. More of a souvenir pressing than a discovery, but the duets still swing.

title: சூறாவளி "Cyclone"
label: Good Morning Tapes
description: Dechery turns up on Good Morning Tapes with a two, part mix drawn from Tamil film music, issued as a limited mixtape. Closer to a curatorial dispatch than a club tool, and very much in keeping with the label's slow, burn cassette catalogue.

title: Analog Fingerprints Vol. 0
label: Numbers.
description: Marco Passarani turns up on Numbers. with eight tracks of analog, rig electro and techno, the kind of hardware, led Roman science he has been refining since the Final Frontier days. For anyone keeping a Lory D shelf nearby.

title: Chainless
label: Young And Cold Records
description: Four tracks of coldwave on Young And Cold, the German label that has been quietly cataloguing this corner of post, punk for years. Test pressing on white label 12", shelve near Tearful Moon.

title: Madeleine
label: Knekelhuis
description: Twelve tracks of art, rock, folk and synth, pop bent into experimental shapes, landing on Knekelhuis where that kind of stylistic drift always finds a home. Sits comfortably alongside the label's Sissi Rada end of the catalogue.

title: State Of Grace
label: Hellcat Records
description: Boston street punk vets back on Hellcat for an eleven, track LP of working, class Oi! and melodic hardcore, pressed in limited reissue form. Shelve next to Dropkick Murphys if you need the obvious pointer.

title: Oda
label: Mondoj
description: Vic Bang's full, length for Mondoj sits in the abstract end of the label's catalogue, eight tracks of experimental electronics issued on limited LP. For listeners already keeping pace with the Mondoj run.

title: Move Your Body (Lee Foss & Micah Baxter Remix)
label: Helix Records (7)
description: Lee Foss and Micah Baxter take a pass at the Chicago house anthem, landing on Helix as a digital single. The kind of update built for current club rotation rather than the archive.

title: Cry Baby
label: Atlantic
description: Atlantic gives the 2015 Martinez debut an LP pressing, seventeen tracks of nursery, rhyme alt, pop wired into trap percussion and brittle synth, pop. A foundational document for the cohort that followed her into the charts.

title: पर्वत (The Mountain)
label: Kong (7)
description: Fifteen, track Gorillaz LP through their own Kong imprint, the genre map (Latin pop, Indo, pop, indie and alt, pop strands) suggesting Damon Albarn is again routing the cartoon band through whichever scenes have caught his ear. Business as usual, which has rarely meant predictable.

title: Bass Is The Space
label: Ilian Tape
description: re:ni links up with BiggaBush for a four, tracker on Ilian Tape, weighting the Zenker brothers' usual techno remit toward sound system dub and UK bass pressure. A 45 RPM 12" for the Pessimist crowd.

artist: Kassel Jaeger & Stephan Mathieu & Akira Rabelais
title: Zauberberg
label: Shelter Press
description: A reissue of the three, way Shelter Press session for processed field recordings and slowly decaying tone, two long pieces that sit closer to acousmatic composition than ambient. For anyone who wore through the original pressing or anything on Kesh.

artist: Nightmares On Wax Vs Adrian Sherwood
title: Flippin' Eck
label: Warp Records
description: George Evelyn handed over to Adrian Sherwood for a versioning job, which is about as logical a pairing as Warp has greenlit in a while. Two tracks of trip hop dragged through On, U Sound's mixing desk; shelve near Smith & Mighty.

title: Kinds
label: Warp Records
description: Kwes. heads to Warp with nine pieces of ambient leaning electronic, a quieter register than the pop production work he is better known for. Sits comfortably alongside the more song, shaped end of the label's roster.

title: PAN 003
label: Pan Records (24)
description: Four, track deep house compilation on Pan Records, the third in the catalogue and the kind of unhurried 12" you file alongside the steadier end of the Quintessentials roster.

title: Street Druid
label: AD 93
description: Eight tracks from the London saxophonist on AD 93, pulling his horn through dub techno haze, electroacoustic drift and a loose future, jazz pulse. Sits comfortably next to Beatrice Dillon for anyone working that side of the label.

title: All Things Might Spill
label: Shelter Press
description: Eight pieces of drone and contemporary ambient from Chantal Michelle, landing on Shelter Press where this kind of patient, slightly austere composition has long had a home. Sits comfortably alongside Félicia Atkinson on the shelf.

title: I Feel Alive
label: Musique TOPS
description: Eleven tracks of soft, focus indie pop from the Montreal group, repressed on their own Musique TOPS imprint. Their AM, radio touch and breezy songcraft remain the draw, file alongside Men I Trust.

title: Otonoma
label: Thrill Jockey
description: Hirano lands on Thrill Jockey with ten pieces of piano, leaning electroacoustic work, the kind of patient ambient and modern classical writing she has built across the last decade. For listeners who keep Hatakeyama and Ian William Craig within reach.

title: Stardust
label: Warp Records
description: Brown back on Warp with a fourteen, track set that, per the tags, leans further into electro and hyperpop than the rap purists will want. Closer in spirit to the Atrocity Exhibition lineage than to Quaranta, with the sugar dialled up.

title: It's Immaterial
label: Ghostly International
description: Ghostly reissues the Chris Stewart project's gauzy synth, pop on vinyl, eleven tracks of coldwave drift sung from somewhere behind the drum machine. For anyone whose Cure and New Order shelves keep wandering toward Sacred Bones.

title: Αν Είχαν Τ' Άστρα Δάκρυα
label: Heaven OST
description: A single tied to the Heaven OST imprint, sitting in the Greek folk lineage rather than anywhere club, adjacent. File alongside the more austere end of Mediterranean vocal records.

title: The Flicker
label: Ruined By Numbers
description: Two long, form drone pieces from the Mertens and Steenkiste pairing, issued in a limited edition on Ruined By Numbers. Patient, acoustic, leaning experimental work for anyone tracking the quieter edges of the Belgian minimalist circuit.

title: Masquerade
label: So Young Records
description: Ten tracks of guitar, led indie rock from the Irish five, piece on So Young, a label whose roster (Folly Group, English Teacher) tends to favour songwriting with some grit under the fingernails. Worth a listen if you've been keeping tabs on that scene.

title: And So It Is
label: Leaving Records
description: Eight tracks of spiritual and contemporary jazz from Aaron Shaw, arriving on Leaving Records in a limited LP pressing. Sits comfortably alongside the label's Carlos Niño orbit.

title: Blasé Saint
label: Sferic
description: Eight pieces of ambient for Sferic, the Manchester label whose roster has quietly defined a certain washed, room, tone strain of the genre. File alongside Loris S. Sarid or Ulla if you need bearings.

title: Chernobyl Gesture
label: Bearded Punk Records
description: Thirteen tracks of melodic pop punk from Brookhurst, landing on Belgium's Bearded Punk for the LP. Straight, ahead stuff for the Epitaph and Fat Wreck shelf, no apologies offered.

title: Nothing But Fixes
label: Modern Love
description: Four tracks of bass, grime and techno pressed at 45 for Modern Love, the Manchester label continuing its long flirtation with sound, system weight. Steel yourself for something closer to Rainy Miller's orbit than the label's ambient wing.

title: Rich EP
label: Lapsus Music
description: Four tracks of straightforward club house from Strieder for Lapsus, the Barcelona imprint that tends toward the deeper, dubbier end of the floor. Functional rather than showy.

title: I Wanna Be Your Dog Again
label: Them Hellas
description: Duckwrth in his looser, funk, leaning mode, a single sitting closer to the soul, pop side of his catalog than to straight rap. Self, released through Them Hellas.

title: Trying Times
label: Good Boy Records (6)
description: Blake on his own Good Boy imprint, leaning further into the ambient register that has shadowed his vocal records for years. Thirteen tracks, limited LP, more inward than the pop framing suggests.

title: Mastery Quantum Sound
label: Houndstooth
description: A twelve, track ambient compilation on Houndstooth, pressed in a limited LP run. The label has been quietly building this side of its catalogue for years, and the format here suggests something closer to a curated set than a sampler.

title: American Hunger (Lunch)
label: Vinyl Digital
description: One of three sequels to MF Grimm's notorious 60, track triple LP, twenty cuts of plainspoken, politically alert New York rap getting a Vinyl Digital pressing. For listeners who stuck with the original American Hunger across all three discs.

title: Πεπρωμένο Μου
label: Heaven OST
description: Stavros Siolas turns up on Heaven OST with a single that sits on the folk side of the label's catalogue rather than its club one. File alongside the more song, shaped corners of the roster.

title: Natural Selection
label: Pan (3)
description: Hecker returns to PAN with nine pieces of psychoacoustic abstraction, the kind of granular, room, warping computer music he has been building out for two decades. Difficult listening that rewards a good pair of speakers.

title: For Almost Ever
label: Scat Records (2)
description: Six tracks of Cleveland power, pop and punk from the Mice, returning via Scat, the label that has long looked after Robert Pollard adjacent Ohio guitar music. File next to Guided By Voices if you need a shelf.

title: ISS012
label: Ilian Tape
description: A electronic EP from Skee Mask, released via Ilian Tape. Pending final write-up.

title: Ultra Villain
label: NAFF
description: Maara (2)'s latest album on NAFF occupies the electronic space. Editorial copy still in draft.

title: In The Red
label: Snappy Little Numbers
description: New single from The Gamits, out on Snappy Little Numbers. Sits in the rock corner. Preview description pending editorial review.

title: Kansai Botanicals
label: Quiet Details
description: Album by Deadbeat on Quiet Details. Filed under electronic. Holding slot for the real description.

title: Eeeeeeee
label: Short Span
description: Picture (6) returns with a EP through Short Span, the kind of electronic that rewards a second listen. Editorial copy still to come.
